subject: general
question: The angle of elevation of the unfinished tower is 45° from a point 45 m away from the base of the tower. After the tower is finished, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the same point becomes 60°. Find the height of the newly built part (√3 = 1.732).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of the newly built part = Distance × (tan θ₂ − tan θ₁)

⇒ Height = 45 × (tan 60° − tan 45°)

⇒ Height = 45 × (√3 − 1)

⇒ Height = 45 × (1.732 − 1) = 45 × 0.732 = 32.94 m

⇒ 32.94 m ≈ 33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 33 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance from the base of the tower (AB) = 45 m

Angle of elevation of the unfinished tower (∠CBA) = 45°

Angle of elevation of the finished tower (∠DBA) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculation:**

In right-angled ΔCAB:

⇒ tan 45° = AC ÷ AB

⇒ 1 = AC ÷ 45

⇒ AC = 45 m

In right-angled ΔDAB:

⇒ tan 60° = AD ÷ AB

⇒ √3 = AD ÷ 45

⇒ AD = 45√3 m

Height of the newly built part (CD) = AD − AC

⇒ CD = 45√3 − 45 = 45(√3 − 1)

⇒ CD = 45 × (1.732 − 1)

⇒ CD = 45 × 0.732 = 32.94 m

⇒ 32.94 m ≈ 33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 33 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when the observer is looking upwards at an object.

Standard Trigonometric Values

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. These are frequently used in heights and distances problems to relate distances directly to height ratios.

Common Heights & Distances Formula

When two angles of elevation θ₁ and θ₂ are observed from the same point at a distance 'd' to an increasing height, the difference in height can be directly calculated using the formula: d × (tan θ₂ − tan θ₁).
